prompt:
Scene:
Create a square product photograph of a math manipulative tray viewed from above on a clean table, with soft side light emphasizing wood, silicone, and card-stock textures. The image should feel premium enough for an education catalog yet approachable enough for classroom use. Keep the square frame balanced, calm, and production-ready so the asset can serve gallery review, research comparison, and real educational delivery at the same time.

Subject:
Include counters, pattern blocks, fraction circles, sorting bowls, and a few companion concept cards arranged in a clear hierarchy. Each object should communicate a specific learning purpose through shape and grouping rather than through printed symbols. The subject arrangement should feel complete and self-contained, able to stand alone as a real supporting deliverable inside the same education business line.

Important details:
Keep the presentation disciplined and highly legible. The assortment should feel intentionally curated for concept transfer across counting, sorting, and patterning, showing that the card system can extend into tactile learning tools. Keep the visual hierarchy modular, commercially believable, and clearly tied to a real educational use case rather than a generic mood board.

Use case:
Math Concept Visual Card Set single study 1/5, manipulative tray.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no readable equations, no numerals, no logos, no messy classroom clutter, no generic stock-photo styling, no broken manipulatives.
